## Computational Assignment Markdown

In this markdown, we analyse the provided ScanRecords.csv file and determine the unknown elements of the data.

```{r imports, echo=FALSE}
# first, need to import relevant packages and set the seed for our random processes
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

set.seed(333)

data <- read.csv("ScanRecords.csv")

# we convert the fraction of hours into minutes/hours in case we want to use it like this
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Minutes = (Duration * 60)
  )
data

```

# Data Exploration

We have a few things we know about the data:

+ All series are independent and identically distributed
+ Patient 1:
    - The duration of scans are normally distributed
    - Patients arrive according to a Poisson distribution 

Let's first explore the data a little. Our focus is to find how the duration and arrival time are distributed, so we consider them first. 
We start with the duration of scans.

```{r}
# look at how the duration of scans for each patient are spread
# use dplyr since it makes the data into a table dataframe automatically, makes it easier to work with
# for now use Minutes instead of Duration, but can switch it to Duration for equivalent results
dura <- data %>%
  group_by(PatientType) %>%
  summarise(
    SD = sd(Minutes),
    Max = max(Minutes),
    Qrt3 = quantile(Minutes, probs = 0.75),
    Mean = mean(Minutes),
    Qrt1 = quantile(Minutes, probs = 0.25),
    Min = min(Minutes)
  )
dura

# make the boxplot of the duration and the summary stats we find
boxDura <- ggplot(data, aes(x = PatientType, y = Minutes, fill = PatientType)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "MRI Scan Durations by Patient Type", 
       x = "Patient Type", 
       y = "Duration (minutes)") +
  stat_boxplot(geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(data$Duration)), by = 0.25)) +
  theme_minimal()

# want to visualise the statistics together with the boxplot, so use the gridExtra package to place them together
tdura <- t(dura)
duraVisual <- tableGrob(tdura)

grid.arrange(boxDura, duraVisual, ncol = 2, widths = c(2, 1.35))



```
The dots are outliers, which here are categorised as being more than 1.5 times the interquartile range above the third quartile, or below the first quartile.

We can now look at the arrivals.

```{r}
# look at how many of each patient arrive each day
dailyCount <- table(data$Date, data$PatientType)
print(dailyCount)
```
